hero.alt: Hand-coloured 1570 map of Tartary by Abraham Ortelius, with a round title cartouche, tents of the khans, and Japan and the American coast to the east
hero.caption: Abraham Ortelius, Tartariae sive Magni Chami regni typus, first printed 1570. Library of Congress.

trail-cities.alt: Map detail: red town symbols around Samarcand and Bukhara, with the tents of the Great Khan drawn beside them
trail-cities.caption: Towns and the Great Khan's tents on Ortelius's map of Tartary, 1570.

trail-architecture.alt: Map detail: clusters of round felt tents, covered wagons and camels drawn on the steppe
trail-architecture.caption: Tents and wagons on Anthony Jenkinson's map of Russia, Muscovy and Tartary, 1562.

trail-customs.alt: Map detail: a caravan of loaded camels and riders on horseback
trail-customs.caption: A caravan on the Catalan Atlas of 1375.

trail-names.alt: Map detail: a round ornamental cartouche lettered Tartariae sive Magni Chami Regni typus
trail-names.caption: The title cartouche of Ortelius's map: Tartary, or the kingdom of the Great Khan.

trail-outliers.alt: Engraving of a lamb growing on a stalk like a plant, grazing the grass around it
trail-outliers.caption: The vegetable lamb of Tartary, from Henry Lee's book of 1887, redrawn from Johann Zahn (1696). Wikimedia Commons, public domain.
